items.title: Trump's Situation Room meeting on Iran ends without deal

featured_image.name: Trump enters Situation Room to make 'final determination' on Iran

items.description:
President Donald Trump convened a high-stakes meeting in the White House Situation Room on Friday to make what he called a "final determination" on a proposed memorandum of understanding with Iran, but the nearly two-hour session ended without a resolution, according to The New York Times.[1]

The meeting came after Trump announced his plans in a Truth Social post Friday morning, writing, "I will be meeting now, in the Situation Room, to make a final determination". He outlined preconditions for any agreement, insisting that Iran "must agree that they will never have a Nuclear Weapon or Bomb" and that the Strait of Hormuz must "immediately open" to unrestricted shipping with no tolls.[2][3][4][5]

items.title: Trump announces lifting of naval blockade on Iran

featured_image.name: What we know about the US military's blockade of Iran

items.description: President Trump declared on Friday that the U.S. naval blockade of the Strait of Hormuz "will now be lifted," posting the announcement on Truth Social after convening in the White House Situation Room to make what officials described as a "final determination" on the deal with Iran. The announcement follows weeks of fraught negotiations and marks the most concrete step toward ending the nearly three-month conflict between the United States and Iran.[1][2]

items.title: China building 80-plus launch pads near nuclear silos

featured_image.name: China's Nuclear Acceleration Revealed in Satellite Images

items.description:
China is constructing a sprawling network of launch pads, bunkers, and communications nodes near its nuclear missile silos in the remote deserts of its northwest, according to a Reuters analysis of satellite imagery published on Friday.[1][2]

The images reveal more than 80 pads that could be used by China's expanding fleet of mobile missile launchers and air-defense batteries, along with facilities that may support electronic warfare, satellite communication, and command operations, according to three security experts who reviewed the imagery for Reuters.[2]

items.title: Suspected Russian drone strikes building in Romania, injuring two

featured_image.name: In Romania, a drone crashed into a high-rise building; a fire broke out  following an explosion | УНН

items.description:
A suspected Russian attack drone struck a residential apartment building in the Romanian border city of Galati early on May 29, causing an explosion and injuring at least two people, according to Romanian media reports and social media accounts from the scene.[1][2]

The incident occurred during an overnight Russian drone assault targeting Ukraine's Odesa region, which shares a border with Romania's Galati county. Romanian news outlet MediaFax reported that the drone impacted the building, with two people sustaining injuries. Fighter jets were scrambled in response, and Romanian authorities dispatched forensic teams and explosives experts to investigate.[2][1]

items.title: Blue Origin's New Glenn rocket explodes during test at Cape Canaveral

featured_image.name: Blue Origin rocket explodes during an engine-firing test

items.description:
A Blue Origin New Glenn rocket exploded during an engine-firing test at Cape Canaveral Space Force Station on Thursday evening, sending a fireball into the night sky and rattling homes across the surrounding area. No injuries were reported.

The explosion occurred around 9 p.m. at Launch Complex 36, where residents of Cape Canaveral and Cocoa Beach felt tremors and soon flooded social media with images of the blast. Blue Origin confirmed the incident in a brief statement: "We encountered an anomaly during today's hotfire test. We will share updates as we gather more information."[1]

Jeff Bezos responded on X, writing: "It's too early to determine the underlying cause, but we are already investigating. Today has been challenging, but we will reconstruct whatever needs to be rebuilt and resume our flights. It's worth the effort."[1]

items.title: US denies Iran's claim it destroyed American aircraft in Bushehr

featured_image.name: Iran accuses US of ceasefire violation

items.description: Iran's state television reported early Friday that a US aircraft was destroyed in the Jam governorate of Bushehr province in southern Iran, citing local governor Masoud Tangestani. A US official denied the claim to Reuters, stating no American aircraft had been shot down near Bushehr, and no independent confirmation of the Iranian report has emerged.[1][2][3]

items.title: Vance says US and Iran 'very close' to ceasefire deal

featured_image.name: US, Iran "very close" to deal to end war, Vance says

items.description:
Vice President JD Vance told reporters on Thursday that the United States and Iran are "very close" to finalizing a memorandum of understanding that would extend their ceasefire for 60 days, reopen the Strait of Hormuz, and restart nuclear discussions — but cautioned the two sides are "not there yet."

The remarks came as Axios reported that US and Iranian negotiators have reached consensus on the terms of the MOU, though the agreement remains unsigned pending approval from President Trump and Iran's supreme leadership. Trump has been briefed on the proposal but has requested "a couple of days" to deliberate before giving his final endorsement.[1][2]
